title: Annotatio IV §.IX: Augustine (2–3) — figure does not remove true presence; presence and participation spiritual
pass_a_gloss: (2) Meanwhile he says the figurative speech of Christ by no means removes from the midst the true presence or participation of His body in the Sacred Supper: Already, says Augustine, Christians celebrate the memory of the sacrifice accomplished, with sacrosanct oblation and participation of the Body and blood of Christ (Against Faustus Book 20 ch. 18, compare ch. 21). But (3.) He makes the Presence and participation of Christ’s Body in the Supper Spiritual: Spiritually, he says, understand what I have spoken (introducing Christ speaking here); For this Body which you see you are about to eat and drink that blood which they will shed who will crucify me — I have committed to you a certain Sacrament; understood SPIRITUALLY it will quicken you (Psalm 98). Also Tractate 25 on John: Why prepare teeth and Belly: Believe and you have eaten.
pass_b_english: Augustine (2): the figure does not remove true presence or participation — Christians celebrate with sacrosanct oblation and participation of Body and blood (Against Faustus 20.18).
(3) Presence and participation are spiritual: understand spiritually; the sacrament understood spiritually quickens (Ps. 98). Tract. 25 John: Why prepare teeth and belly? Believe, and you have eaten.
source_text: (2) Figuratam interim Christi locutionem, veram corporis ejus in Cœna S., vel præsentiam, vel participationem, neutiquam è medio tollere dicit: Jam, ait Augustinus, Christiani, peracti sacrificii memoriam, celebrant, sacrosanctâ oblatione & participatione Corporis & sanguinis Christi, Lib. 20. contra Faustum cap. 18. confer. cap. 21. At verò (3.) Præsentiam atque participationem Corporis Christi in Cœna, Spirituales facit: Spiritualiter inquit, intelligite quæ locutus sum (Christum hic loquentem introducens); Nam hoc Corpus, quod videtis, manducaturi estis & bibituri illum sanguinem, quem fusuri sunt, qui me crucifigent, Sacramentum vobis aliquod commendavi, SPIRITUALITER intellectum vivificabit vos in Psalm. 98. Item Tractatu 25. in Johannem: Ut quid paras dentes & Ventrem: Crede & manducasti.

lemmas.gloss: by no means remove from the midst
